newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Japan tariffs to squeeze Taiwan feed, pork prices.
newsitem.headline: Japan tariffs to squeeze Taiwan feed, pork prices.

text.p: Tokyo's three-month emergency tariff on imported pork from January 1 will squeeze already-weak feed and pork prices in Taiwan, Japan's top supplier, local pork producers said on Thursday.
"Taiwan's pork prices have already fallen over 40 percent from their June highs," Taiwan Frozen Meat Packers Association chairman Hsu Hsin-Sung told Reuters by telephone.
"Japan's new tariff will add pressure on us."
Taiwan's average wholesale pork price on Thursday was around T$41 per kg, down from a peak of T$72 per kg in early June.
Taiwan's Council of Agriculture officials attributed the sharp fall primarily to Japan's reimposition on July 1 of a pork import tariff at a time of generally strong production in Taiwan.

The emergency tariff, permitted under international trade rules, would raise the duty on pork carcasses to 6.4 percent from 4.8 percent for imports with a value of greater than 565.70 yen per kg. The tariff is in place for three months.
Hsu said Taiwan breeders could cut back on pig numbers to ensure local prices after the traditional Chinese New Year in February, which is expected to boost local pork consumption.
"We now hope the Chinese New Year can add more pork consumption," Hsu said.
Hsu said breeders would have to cut back further on pig numbers after the Chinese New Year to ensure supplies are in line with demand.
Taiwan grain traders said trimming pig numbers would add long-term pressure to feed consumption and local corn prices.
Taiwan corn prices on Thursday were at around T$5.5, down from late October highs of about T$6.3 per kg, grain traders said. Recent corn import costs were around 4.7 per kg.
Of Taiwan's 266,757 tonnes of pork exports in 1995, 183,494 tonnes -- or 69 percent -- went to Japan, which has been the island's largest pork market by a wide margin.
Japan's frozen and refrigerated pork imports in November rose 29.6 percent to 31,399 tonnes from the same month in 1995. More than half of the imported pork was from Taiwan.
